claims.statement: Pataliputra was the Mauryan capital. The Greek envoy Megasthenes described a city defended by a timber wall, gates and towers. That account gives us a view of the capital through a visitor’s writing. It should not be treated as a complete description of everyday life there.

Pataliputra under the Mauryas: 321 BCE to 185 BCE. Editorial window follows the dynasty, not the foundation or end of the city. Megasthenes’ description is literary testimony. A precise map reference has not yet been checked.

Kumrahar archaeological site reference within Pataliputra. This point locates the existing study window; it does not date every structure, define the city’s boundaries or establish any person’s presence.
